subject: Post-demo: vector eval & next steps for SearchLytics
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: vector eval & next steps for SearchLytics

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can lock in a pilot plan: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve semantic search recall for long-tail docs (internal KB + product pages) and reduce false positives on legal/regulatory pages.
- Current setup: Elasticsearch + in-house 512-d embeddings (dense index), periodic reindex weekly.
- Constraints: DOCS are ~120M docs (mostly text + metadata), want >95% uptime, and a target p95 latency under 120ms for top-K=10 queries.

Preliminary model recommendations
- Baseline: RWI-Emb-512 (current production) — used as the control for any AB tests.
- Candidate 1 (recommended): OpenEmbed-2.7B-SEM-512-quant — good tradeoff of throughput and semantic lift, expected +6–10% recall@10 on our sample.
- Candidate 2 (higher-quality): RWI-Emb-768-finetune — higher dimensionality, better cluster separation; consider if storage and index cost acceptable.

Key metrics to validate (what we'll measure during pilot)
- Recall@10, MRR@10, and precision@5 on the SearchLytics query set (10k sampled queries).
- Drift signal: cosine shift over time + per-document embedding variance.
- Dimensionality trade: PCA explained variance ratio for 256/512/768 subspace comparisons.

Attachments and links
- Attached: searchlytics-demo-notes.pdf (call notes), sem-bench-results-v1.csv (quick sample bench), prompt-sets-sample.jsonl (sample prompts for reranking).
- Bench folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-benchmarks

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) You approve a 10k-query sample and share a 1% random doc sample snapshot (CSV with id, text, metadata) — due Tue 12/09.
2) Redwood runs a 2-week embedding evaluation (RWI-Emb-512 baseline vs OpenEmbed-2.7B-SEM-512-quant) with our semantic metric suite — results by 12/23.
3) If candidate wins on recall/latency, run a gated AB roll to 10% traffic in your staging environment.

Cost and retention notes
- Quick estimate: evaluation CPU/GPU costs for the 2-week run ~ $5–8k (depends on exact sampling), full pilot scale numbers after we confirm index size and retention.
- Data retention: we do not persist raw queries in hosted evaluation; embeddings and metrics are retained per your policy. We can accommodate custom retention for Private/Dedicated.

Alyssa — if that schedule looks OK I’ll kick off the sampling request and loop procurement for an MSA addendum if needed.

Thanks,
Jordan
Sales | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: searchlytics-demo-notes.pdf (10 pages), sem-bench-results-v1.csv (sample 1k rows), prompt-sets-sample.jsonl (50 items)

Jordan / Karthik — quick internal note on the evaluation plan:

- Sampling: 10k queries is good; request stratified sampling so we cover head (top 1k queries), mid-tail (next 4k), and long-tail (remaining 5k). This will surface drift and long-tail lift.
- Metrics: we should add intra-query diversity score (avg cosine distance between top-5 results) and clustering purity on labeled subset (they mentioned some labeled legal docs).
- Dimensionality experiment: run baseline 512, candidate 512, and candidate 768 but measure index size delta and retrieval latency. For RWI-Emb-768 estimate index size +45% vs 512 — flagging for cost conversation.
- Cost estimate: rough infra for the 2-week test on Redwood Dedicated (spot + burst) — $7,200 (includes embedding recompute + similarity search benchmarking across both models). Add 15% margin for retries/data prep.

Karthik — can you prepare a short sample script (python) that takes SearchLytics CSV and returns eval metrics and PCA explained variance plot? Jordan, once Alyssa confirms sample we'll run the job in our staging bucket.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa / Procurement team — following up with the requested clarifications and a one-line cost estimate for procurement: 

1) Serving requirement: OpenEmbed-2.7B-SEM-512-quant will run on CPU for offline evaluation (embedding recompute and batch encode) but for online low-latency serving we recommend GPU-backed instances to meet the p95 <120ms target under realistic load. For the pilot evaluation (our 2-week bench) we will run bulk encoding on GPU nodes to speed the job; similarity queries during metric collection can run on CPU.

2) One-line cost estimate for procurement: Estimated Redwood eval spend (2-week embedded recompute + full bench across two candidate models): $7,200 (approx). This excludes any changes to your production search cluster costs.

3) Data retention: For the evaluation we will store: embeddings (kept up to 30 days by default), raw query logs (redacted after metric extraction), and aggregated metrics (retained indefinitely in your account unless you request deletion). We can mirror your retention policy for Private/Dedicated deployments — happy to add a short clause to the SOW.

Links & artifacts: 
- Bench folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-benchmarks (includes sem-bench-results-v1.csv and prompt-sets-sample.jsonl)
- Live eval dashboard (read-only): https://app.redwood.ai/evals/SL-2026-081

Next steps: once we receive the 1% document snapshot (by 12/09) we'll schedule the job for 12/11–12/23 and share mid-point results by 12/17. If procurement needs a short SOW/MAA we can share a 1-page addendum by EOD tomorrow.

Alyssa — want to confirm if SearchLytics prefers the candidate 512 quant model (better cost/perf) or testing the 768 finetune in the same run (will increase CPU/GPU cost and index size). We recommend starting with the 512 quant vs baseline and only escalate to 768 if recall delta is <4% but latency gains are insufficient.

Thanks — Jordan
Redwood Inference
